source.title: How to Code Your FIRST Website (in 10 minutes)

title: Code Your First Website
summary: Build a tiny webpage from scratch with a big heading, bold and slanted words, and some color.
outcome: A one-page website with a dark blue heading, a short introduction about you, and a light blue background.

files.content:
hello world!!!!!

My name is Coder Coder.

I really like coding!

steps.title: What we're building
steps.instruction: Watch the intro. You'll make a real webpage using just a text editor and a web browser.
steps.why: Knowing the goal makes each step make sense.
hints: Nothing to type in this step.

steps.title: Create index.html
steps.instruction: Watch how the file is made. Your project already has a file called index.html, which is where your webpage lives. The browser reads it and shows the page.
steps.why: Every webpage starts as a plain text file ending in .html.

concept.title: HTML and CSS
concept.explain: HTML says what is on the page, like words and headings; CSS says how it looks, like colors and fonts.

links.title: MDN: Getting started with the web

steps.title: Hello world
steps.instruction: Watch the presenter type plain words into the file and see them show up in the browser.
steps.why: It shows that whatever you write in the file appears on the page.
hints: Notice how saving and reloading shows the change.

steps.title: A paragraph with a bold name
steps.instruction:
At the top of index.html, add a paragraph. Start it with

steps.why:
Tags wrap around words to tell the browser what they are:

means a paragraph, means important (bold) words.

checks.say: I can't see a paragraph with a bold name yet.
Write 'My name is' inside your paragraph.

hints: You need a paragraph, and inside it some words plus a bold name.

and closing

. Inside, after 'My name is', wrap your name in and .

concept.title: Tags
concept.explain: A tag is a word in angle brackets; an opening and closing tag wrap around words to give them meaning.

steps.title: A slanted sentence
steps.instruction:
Below your first paragraph's closing

, add a second paragraph. Inside it, write 'I really like coding!' wrapped in and . The tag means 'say this with emphasis' and makes the words slanted (italic).
steps.why: Emphasis helps some words stand out, just like when you stress a word when talking.

checks.say: I can't see your slanted sentence yet.
Write that you like coding in your slanted sentence.

hints: Make another paragraph, this time with slanted words.

After the first

, add

and

, and inside put the sentence between and .

concept.title: Emphasis
concept.explain: The em tag marks words you want to stress, and browsers show them slanted.

steps.title: A big heading
steps.instruction:
At the very top of the file, add a big heading. Start with

, write 'hello world!!!!!' on the next line, and end with

. The h1 tag is the biggest, most important title on a page.
steps.why: Headings give your page a clear title so readers know what it's about.

checks.say: I can't see your big heading yet.
Your heading should say hello world.

hints: Put a big title above everything else.

At the very top, open with

and close with

, with 'hello world!!!!!' in between.

concept.title: Headings
concept.explain: Heading tags go from h1, the biggest title, down to h6, the smallest.

steps.title: Color the background
steps.instruction: At the very top of the file, add <style> and </style>. Between them, write a rule for body (the whole page) that sets background to lightblue. The style tag holds CSS, the language for how things look.
steps.why: CSS lets you change colors and fonts without touching your words.

checks.say: I can't see your style section yet.
Your page background isn't light blue yet.

hints: Add a place for styling at the top, then make the whole page light blue.
Use <style> and </style>. Inside, write body, curly brackets, and the background property set to lightblue, ending with a semicolon.

concept.title: CSS rules
concept.explain: A CSS rule names what to style, then lists changes inside curly brackets, like background: lightblue;

steps.title: Style the heading
steps.instruction: Inside the style section, below the body rule's closing }, add a rule for h1. Set font-family to Arial (the letter shape) and color to darkblue (the text color).
steps.why: Giving the heading its own font and color makes it stand out.

checks.say: Your heading isn't dark blue yet.
Your heading isn't using the Arial font yet.

hints: Make a second rule, this time just for the big heading.
After the body rule, write h1 with curly brackets. Inside, set font-family to Arial and color to darkblue.

concept.title: Fonts and colors
concept.explain: font-family picks the letter style and color picks the text color.

steps.title: You built a website!
steps.instruction: Watch the wrap-up. Try changing the colors or words to make the page your own.
steps.why: Playing with your code is the best way to learn.
hints: Try swapping lightblue for another color.

quiz.question: Which language changes how your page looks?
quiz.explain: HTML holds the content, CSS sets colors and fonts.
